mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.75% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% over a three-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which compresses earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS below their 12-month averages over two months indicates a synchronized weakening in labor market participation and income, which reduces aggregate demand and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both fall below 12-month moving averages for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS are below their 12-month averages for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
